title: Fitting singular subscheme of a nodal relative curve
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension $1$ and has only ordinary double point singularities (equivalently, at a singular geometric point its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ for an algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$). Let $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the relative smooth locus $U\subset X$ is open and the underlying set of $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ is $X\setminus U$; $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\to S$ is unramified. For every morphism $S'\to S$, if $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is the base change, then the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $f'$ is canonically $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_SS'$ and its underlying set is the nonsmooth locus of $f'$.

proof.text: First establish the formation assertion for an arbitrary base change $S'\to S$. On affine charts [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the base-changed ring with $A'=R'\otimes_R A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], $\Omega_{A'/R'}\cong A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/R}$. If $\Omega_{A/R}=A^n/K$, the tensor product is $A'^n/\langle\operatorname{image}K\rangle$: maps out of either quotient are exactly the balanced maps from $A'\times(A^n/K)$, so this identification follows directly from the tensor-product universal property. Thus the new relation module is generated by the images of the old relations. Multilinearity of determinants shows that its $(n-1)$-minors generate exactly $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{A/R})A'$, including the unit-ideal convention for $n\leq1$. By [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme] these are the defining ideals, so the affine equalities glue and give $\operatorname{Sing}(f')=\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_S S'$ as closed subschemes, canonically over $X'=X\times_SS'$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] to $f$ with $d=1$. Its flatness and local-finite-presentation hypotheses are those of the item, and its pure geometric-fibre dimension hypothesis is exactly the dimension assumption here; empty fibres are expressly allowed. For $d=1$ its closed subscheme is $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ by [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. It follows that the relative smooth locus $U$ is open and $|\operatorname{Sing}(f)|=|X|\setminus U$.

Write $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$. The composite $Z\to S$ is locally of finite type: on an affine chart $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra since it is finitely presented, and the closed subscheme has ring $A/I$, generated over $R$ by the images of the generators of $A$ ([def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]). For any geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, step 1 identifies $Z_{\bar s}$ with the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $C=X_{\bar s}$. If $C$ is empty its singular subscheme is empty and unramified by the definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Otherwise clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives that $C$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type over $\Omega$; it is pure of dimension one and at worst nodal by hypothesis. Apply implication (1) to (2) of [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$: it gives that $Z_{\bar s}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is unramified. Hence [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion], applied to the locally finite type morphism $Z\to S$, proves that it is unramified.

proof.text: For arbitrary $S'\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] give that $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. If $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S'$ is a geometric point, the fibre-product universal property identifies its geometric fibre with $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, using the composite geometric point $\bar t\to S$. Thus every nonempty such fibre is pure of dimension one by the original hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] with $d=1$ to $f'$: its first-Fitting singular subscheme has support equal to its nonsmooth locus. Together with the canonical closed-subsheme equality of step 1 this gives both assertions after arbitrary base change. No reduction of a closed subscheme is taken.
